To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we can achieve a 2x improvement in energy efficiency by designing a quasi-specific processor core for a particular workload and (ii) we can achieve this improvement by trading off performance and power efficiency.

(1) the energy efficiency of a processor can be improved by trading off some performance for a higher percentage of dark silicon, and (2) the performance loss can be mitigated by utilizing the dark silicon to design specialized quasi-specific cores that optimize energy per computation.
We present QSCORES, a scalable energy-efficient processor architecture that uses quasi-specific cores to exploit the dark silicon of modern microprocessors.

developing a methodology for designing quasi-specific cores, and evaluating their energy efficiency in the presence of dark silicon.
designing a scalable energy efficient core that is optimized for a specific class of applications.
